newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases on futures in sluggish market.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases on futures in sluggish market.

text.p: NWE gas oil edged lower on Friday as benchmark IPE gas oil headed lower and demand remained sluggish, traders said.
July IPE gas oil settled $1.0 lower at $158.50 a tonne lower, some $4.0 below last Friday's closing price.
"It was a typical Friday no-one's interested," said one trader.
"Until futures show signs that they have really bottomed out buyers aren't going to come back in," another trader said.

The heating oil barge market was fairly quiet. A couple of parcels of storage material traded at around July IPE -75 cents fob ARA, while running refinery was done at around July IPE -50 cents fob ARA.

Low sulphur diesel was also in doldrums as over-supply continued to pressure the market. Barge premiums were quoted around July IPE +$4.50/+$5.50 fob ARA. Material was offered out of Antwerp at July IPE +$4.75.

On the cargo front, EN590 cargoes were quoted at July IPE +$5.0/+$5.50. Traders said the market remained well-supplied as material continued to arrive from outside the area and arbitrage doors out of the region remained shut.
In the 0.2 percent front, premiums were firmly ensconced in negative territory with Russian talked around -$1.0/flat cif NWE. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
